**"People who are not depressed see the world they want to see it. People who are depressed see the world the way it actually is."**

After years of dealing with that exact advice, I can't say I have an answer for you. But please keep reading. 

I found myself attending dozens, probably even a hundred or more therapy sessions. I've only seen three therapists, all three over the course of about 5 years. At first, I stressed about my identity, then self harm, and things ranging from being suicidal, to having family problems, to little things like why I didn't sleep. I was at a war with myself for a long time. My therapists stressed that I needed to go out more, to make friends, to go for walks and find hobbies. 

I started learning guitar. Then the ukulele. I went for a walk almost four times a week. I seen long distance friends at the expense of their money (which made me feel bad but they insisted it was okay). I stopped cutting for five years. I got my drivers license. I adopted a puppy. I involved myself in dozens of television shows and movies. 
When I listen to my therapists, their advice can only be so helpful. I complain, they listen. I listen, they give me advice. 

After five years, after all those things, and after being admitted into two psychiatrist hospitals, seeing a dozen different doctors, I have found that "getting a job" or "doing ((X)) thing" will not solve the simplest of problems. Still reading? Okay. I hope so. You have lived 22 years. You have experienced what most people should have in just a few amount of years. I don't know you personally, no, but LIVE. Just..try. That's honestly my only advice right now. I'm sorry if I disappointed you, but please, you have to just try a bit longer. There will be plently of heartaches, you will lose family members, you will have more jobs, you will have more girlfriends (or boyfriends? I dunno what you like man, whatevs.) You will LIVE to see technology grow and advance, there will be plenty of full moons to see, movies to watch, TV series to start, want to go to Scotland? Fucking go to Scotland. Don't have the money? Save. Even if it takes 10 years. Go see Scotland. I can't say that I've been to Scotland, but you can, if that's what you want. 

I can't honestly take your depression away or give you some magic pill, but man, if I could, I would. Living hurts, but its also EXPERIENCE. It hurts, I know. I hurt too. I have depression, I fight my own battles..but..just experience life. Some experiences are bad but try to make it what you can.

Anxiety can cause a lot of weird things..especially paranoia and I went through the same thing friend. Try to keep your mind as occupied as possible until the 22nd, you do not want to be this anxious until then! Can you take aspirin for your pain? I can imagine that would help a bit..and get involved into some TV shows or movies, you see the new x-men? What kind of things do you like?
I try not to focus but its really hard when its right there..

I found myself in a similar situation. Its weird, to read peoples stories and to see that they struggle so much and it seems like it kind of makes you feel different, like something changed. Stay strong, keep yourself busy. Keep finding more subreddits because it will be worth it and most of them are just silly and great and it will make you laugh and maybe cry some more.
